note: A listening exercise for a beginner: tap each note against Do to hear home (Ti pulls hardest), tap the two chords that differ by one note, then name major or minor by ear. One staff per step, each showing only the notes that step names; the staff is explained the first time it appears.

exercise.title: Home, and the note that makes major or minor
exercise.focus: Do as home in C · Do-Ti-Do · 1-3-5 vs 1-♭3-5 · major or minor 3rd by ear
exercise.why: Hearing home and hearing major against minor are the two judgements every later ear skill builds on.

sections.text: The staff below shows the C major scale with its solfège names; tap a note to hear it. Tap {{1}}, then {{7}}, and stop: it hangs, as if waiting. Now tap {{1}} {{7}} {{1}}: you are home. Do the same with each other note from {{2}} up to {{6}}: {{1}}, the note, stop. Which ones sound finished, and which want to go back to {{1}}?
One note makes major or minor
Now tap {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}}: C minor. Only the middle note moved, by a half step. Switch between the two staffs, then try it with your eyes closed.
Press Start below. The game plays two notes together, a major 3rd or a minor 3rd: pick the one you heard.
